mechanism: VIP inhibits SST/PV which inhibit pyramidal cells; a context cue activates VIP -> SST/PV silenced -> a specific pyramidal population is transiently DISINHIBITED, opening a context-cued write/read gate (routing, not gain)
citation: Pi/Kepecs 2013 Nature 503:521; Letzkus 2011/2015 disinhibition for fear learning; Williams & Holtmaat 2019 Nat Neurosci 22:1834 'Adaptive disinhibitory gating by VIP permits associative learning'
orthogonal_to_sparse_why: sparse coding changes per-fact CODE DENSITY (k-of-N) uniformly; disinhibition is a SELECTION/ROUTING lever over the write port conditioned on context cue -- it decides WHICH bindings enter WHICH context store, orthogonal to representational density. Capacity wall says 'store can't hold more'; routing says 'don't write the wrong facts into the wrong context'.
adaptive_green_condition: optimal gate-OPEN threshold SHIFTS with context-collision rate rho: LOW-rho -> keep gate OPEN (closing loses recall); HIGH-rho -> gate CLOSES tightly to route by context and avoid cross-context overwrite. A FIXED gate loses one regime. Adaptive carries the majority across the rho-sweep AND does-no-harm at low-rho.
frozen_bar_sketch: K contexts each write B bindings into shared two-store CLS, keys collide at rate rho, recall cued by (context,key). ARMS: DISINHIB / NO-GATE / BEST-FIXED-GATE / ABL(cue-shuffle) / ACH-FROZEN(deconfound). A PRESENCE disinhib-nogate>=+0.10 hi-rho; B EARNED-ADAPTIVE disinhib beats best-FIXED-gate by >=half(disinhib-worstfixed) across rho-sweep; C ABL->collapse; D LOW-rho NO-HARM disinhib>=nogate-0.05; E DECONFOUND survives ACh-gate-frozen-optimal. GREEN iff A^B^C^D^E.
cheapest_refuter: rho-sweep (~5 values x3 seeds, minutes CPU numpy) with BEST-FIXED-GATE arm: if one grid-tuned constant gate fraction captures the lift across all rho (B fails), routing is static-architecture -> 12th-style no-free-lunch -> WALL.

mechanism: PV-basket-cell GABA feedback generates ~40Hz gamma chopping input into discrete time-bins; features in one gamma cycle bind into ONE item, successive cycles kept SEPARATE; nested in theta gives an ordered multi-item buffer
citation: Lisman & Jensen 2013 Neuron 77:1002 'The Theta-Gamma Neural Code'; Buzsaki & Wang 2012 Annu Rev Neurosci 35:203; Bartos/Vida/Jonas 2007 PV gamma
orthogonal_to_sparse_why: TEMPORAL-SEGMENTATION lever, not spatial-density: sparse coding decorrelates SIMULTANEOUS features; gamma decides WHICH features count as simultaneous (one item vs two). A perfect sparse store still cannot decide if stream [a,b,c,d] is one 4-feature binding or two 2-feature bindings -- a segmentation decision sparseness does not make.
adaptive_green_condition: adaptive bin-WIDTH (gamma freq tracks input rate r): fast stream -> narrow bins (segment finely, avoid merging items); slow/bursty -> wide bins (group co-arriving features, avoid fragmenting). A FIXED bin over-merges fast OR over-fragments slow; adaptive wins BOTH ends of the r-sweep.
frozen_bar_sketch: continuous feature STREAM, ground-truth items=variable-length groups of co-arriving features at rate r, NO abrupt boundaries (NE deconfound). ARMS: GAMMA(adaptive bin tracks r) / NO-BIN / BEST-FIXED-BIN / ABL(bins shuffled) / NE-OFF(no boundary so flush provably inert). A PRESENCE gamma-nobin>=+0.10; B EARNED-ADAPTIVE gamma beats best-fixed-bin by >=half across r-sweep; C ABL->collapse; D RATE-SHIFT gamma wins at BOTH hi-r and lo-r where one fixed bin loses; E NE-DECONFOUND zero boundaries -> lift is segmentation not flush. GREEN iff A^B^C^D^E.
cheapest_refuter: r-sweep with BEST-FIXED-BIN: if one grid-tuned bin-width captures segmentation across all rates (B/D fail) -> static window -> WALL. Plus NE-deconfound: if removing abrupt boundaries kills the lift it was NE-flush re-skin -> SKIP. One numpy sweep, minutes.

mechanism: GABA acts DIVISIVELY (not subtractively): response divided by summed activity of a normalization pool, stabilizing gain across input-strength variation
citation: Carandini & Heeger 2012 Nat Rev Neurosci 13:51 'Normalization as a canonical neural computation'; Katzner/Busse/Carandini 2011 J Neurosci 31:5931 GABA_A gain in V1; Silver 2010
orthogonal_to_sparse_why: PARTIAL: normalization rescales MAGNITUDES, sparse re-codes WHICH units active -- different ops, but both are static transforms of the same readout score vector (recall=argmax of M.key).
adaptive_green_condition: normalize match-scores by current total store activity so recall is robust when binding-STRENGTH varies wildly (heavy-tailed). DOUBT: argmax is INVARIANT to monotone rescaling -- a COMMON denominator divides every candidate equally -> argmax UNCHANGED -> INERT on winner-take-all recall (same as H_1533 modern-Hopfield argmax(sim^p)==argmax(sim)). Only PER-CANDIDATE-heterogeneous normalization changes the answer.
frozen_bar_sketch: superposition store, binding-strengths heavy-tailed (some 10x stronger). ARMS: DIVNORM(per-candidate pool-energy divisor) / PLAIN(raw argmax) / BEST-FIXED-GAIN(global divisor grid-tuned) / ABL(const divisor) / SHUFFLE(pool perm). A PRESENCE divnorm-plain>=+0.10 heavy-tail; B EARNED-ADAPTIVE divnorm beats best-fixed-GLOBAL-gain (critical: if global const captures it, argmax-invariance proven -> WALL); C ABL->collapse; D HOMOG-NO-HARM; E per-candidate heterogeneity acts. GREEN iff A^B; WALL likely if best-fixed-global ties.
cheapest_refuter: trivial+decisive: DIVNORM vs BEST-FIXED-GLOBAL-GAIN on same heavy-tail recall -- argmax provably unchanged by common-denominator normalization -> B fails first run -> WALL. Near-instant numpy argmax-invariance check.

mechanism: inhibition homeostatically maintains a target E/I ratio keeping the network near criticality (max info capacity/dynamic range); after a load shock it re-balances back to set-point
citation: Turrigiano 2011 Annu Rev Neurosci homeostatic plasticity; Hengen 2013 firing-rate homeostasis; Ma 2019 bioRxiv criticality as homeostatic set-point
orthogonal_to_sparse_why: WEAKLY: 'maintain store at max-capacity criticality' is nearly the SAME claim as the capacity-optimization H_1551 already tested; the capacity benefit is MONOTONE (best-fixed captures it). Homeostasis FINDS the set-point but does not make the optimum regime-shifting.
adaptive_green_condition: would need a NON-STATIONARY set-point (target E/I itself moves) -- but a set-point is by definition a SINGLE target, the OPPOSITE of a regime-shifting optimum, so a FIXED E/I grid-tuned to it captures the benefit and re-balancing is INERT (H_1528 monotone-resource failure mode). If the target DOES move it collapses into the H_1552 non-stationary lens already in flight, not a new family.
frozen_bar_sketch: ARMS: HOMEO(E/I adapts toward set-point after load shock) / FIXED-EI(grid-tuned const) / ABL(target frozen) / SHUFFLE. Bar B: homeo beats best-FIXED-EI. Expected to tie -> WALL.
cheapest_refuter: grid-tune FIXED-EI at the homeostatic target and compare; by H_1528 precedent (monotone resource -> fixed baseline at adaptive final value ties) expected to tie -> WALL. Free given H_1528 harness pattern.
